claims.claim: A quarter of the authorized police positions (תקנים) in areas with widespread crime are unstaffed
claims.verified_figure: Per Police HR Division data (via Haaretz snippets): Ayalon region (south Tel Aviv, Jaffa, Bat Yam, Holon — the area flagged as higher-crime) is 75% staffed = 25% vacant; Jerusalem district 78% (22% vacant); Tel Aviv district 80% (20% vacant); 23 of 86 stations nationally (~27%) short >20%. National baseline per Knesset RIC 2026: ~92% staffed (~8% vacant), ~1,470 unfilled station positions.
claims.article_figure_per_search_snippet: 'במרחב איילון ... שיעור האיוש מגיע ל־75% בלבד – באזור שסובל מהיקף פשיעה גבוה יותר'; '23 מתוך 86 תחנות בארץ חסרים יותר מ־20% מהשוטרים'; Jerusalem 78%, Tel Aviv 80%
claims.note: Article body unreachable (EGRESS_BLOCKED, premium); judged the headline's own claim only, against article figures surfaced in search snippets. The 'quarter' figure is real but corresponds to a single region (Ayalon, 75% staffed); the headline generalizes it to plural, undefined 'areas with widespread crime'. Other high-crime-adjacent districts cited are lower (Jerusalem 22%, Tel Aviv 20% vacant). 'Areas with widespread crime' is not defined by a stated metric, and the data is not public, so the denominator cannot be checked. Directionally correct (well above the ~8% national vacancy baseline), hence imprecise rather than overstated. Note also a separate figure — 23/86 stations (~a quarter of stations) short >20% — that a reader could conflate with 'a quarter of positions'. Not 'source_unreadable' since the underlying figures are surfaced and consistent; the HR dataset itself is non-public.
